0.long_answer: Prostaglandin E1 is the medication used to keep the ductus arteriosus open in newborns with tricuspid atresia. This treatment is vital because, in cases of congenital heart defects like tricuspid atresia, the ductus arteriosus allows for necessary blood flow between the aorta and the pulmonary artery until corrective surgical procedures can be performed. By preventing the ductus arteriosus from closing, prostaglandin E1 maintains adequate oxygenation and circulation in the neonate.
